highlights.narrative: Customers reported being locked out of their accounts and unable to complete actions such as making online payments or logging in. Some cases involved lost passwords with an inability to reset them, while others reflected being blocked from opening new accounts due to reporting on their file. The lockouts spanned both access-credential failures and account-eligibility restrictions.

evidence.text: I could not make further payments when attempted on XX/XX/XXXX, as my account was locked to login and could not make an online payment.
My account password has been lost and I am unable to reset the password.
Since then, I have been unable to open any bank accounts due to the report on my XXXX XXXX XXXX file.

highlights.narrative: Customers raised disputes over fees they contend were unwarranted, including a charged airline change fee escalated to their card issuer and a charge for extra service time that had been explicitly canceled with verbal staff agreement. In both cases the complainant is contesting a specific charged amount and seeking review or reversal.

evidence.text: On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the BOA customer service team through both a phone call and an email regarding a {$270.00} airline change fee from XXXX XXXX XXXX, charged to my BOA XXXX XXXX XXXX credit card ending in XXXX.
The business charged us for an extra XXXX minutes of karaoke time that we explicitly canceled and which staff verbally agreed.

highlights.narrative: Across the eligible interactions, a substantial share involved customers reporting fraud, unauthorized transactions, or identity theft who were then denied relief or redirected rather than having their claims resolved. Cases include disputed card charges deemed authorized, denied unauthorized ATM transaction claims, and unemployment fraud tied to stolen identity. The pattern reflects fraud victims being turned away or shifted elsewhere after raising legitimate fraud concerns.

Unauthorized atm transactions field complaint with my bank I was denied XXXX $

Covid-19 pandemic unemployment insurance with bank of America I was informed by the IRS a claim was filed in my name of {$19000.00} from California my identity was stolen .this matter has been disappointing all this time I could not file for unemployment because someone has use my information already.

highlights.narrative: Customers report that funds were frozen, held, or otherwise made inaccessible by the institution, in several cases without prior notice or clear explanation. Instances include account access being blocked around an account closure, an unexplained hold placed on transferred funds, and money withheld amid delays in resolving an uncashable check. The finding was flagged in a subset of eligible interactions.

evidence.text: I didnt even realize BOA had blocked my account access until about XXXX days since the deposit had passed, when I tried to login to my account after receiving an account closure letter.
When I went to the atm to do the withdrawal I had to go in my bank app to do a transfer from my business account to my personal account I noticed the XXXX hold on my account for {$4000.00}.
Return my money reissue an unable to deposit expired check with interests from their unnecessary uncooperative delays {$51.00} still has not been returned yet of many years now.

highlights.narrative: Across the flagged interactions, customers reported that payments were not applied as expected, including funds never reaching the beneficiary bank, a check reversed after being processed under the wrong currency, and payments posting late despite use of an automatic on-time payment system. The pattern reflects payments being misapplied, delayed, or reversed after submission. These accounts describe outcomes where the customer's payment did not credit correctly.

evidence.text: ( Please see the attached document labeled XXXX XXXX XXXX. ) As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX than XXXX months laterthe funds have still not been received by the beneficiary bank.
Bank of America later informed me that the check was incorrectly processed under the wrong currency and subsequently reversed.

I explained to the representative that my payments are posting late dispite utilzing their automatic system that states if you make a payment on the due date at XXXXXXXX XXXX the payment will post that day.

highlights.narrative: Across the eligible interactions, remediation was denied in a substantial share of cases, with customers reporting that requested fraud protection, reimbursement, refund tracing, or trace documentation was refused or claimed to be unavailable. Institutions denied fraud reimbursement, asserted an inability to locate or track funds sent to closed accounts, and refused to provide reference numbers or trace documentation for refund transactions.

evidence.text: I contacted BOA, seeking fraud protection or reimbursement, and that was denied by the bank.
However, when I contacted Bank of America, they claimed they could not locate the funds and insisted that they had no way to track refunds sent to a closed account.
XXXX refuses to provide the ARN ( Acquirer Reference Number ) or any trace documentation for the refund transaction.

highlights.narrative: The rubric item repeat_complaint_unresolved was flagged across a substantial share of eligible interactions, indicating customers returning after a prior complaint or claim went unaddressed. Evidence shows consumers explicitly referencing earlier CFPB cases and denied claims, signaling that initial resolution attempts failed to satisfy the complaint. The pattern reflects escalation of unresolved issues rather than newly originated grievances.
